content.title: Hundreds of thousands gather in South Boston for St. Patrick's Day parade
content.text: Boston's St. Patrick's Day Parade kicked off Sunday as nearly 1 million people gathered in South Boston for the popular celebration.New security tactics to help keep attendees safe were unleashed Sunday, including drones, set to help prevent overcrowding on rooftops and balconies, but also provide security in the midst of the Iran War and potential acts of terrorism."Given the size of the crowd, some incidents that have happened outside of the state, around the country, we want to be sure we have the eyes and ears to respond to things in real time as fast as possible," Massachusetts State Sen. Nick Collins said.Boston police officers were in full force Sunday, cracking down on public drinking. "This isn't Mardi Gras, we don't want it to be," said Bob Ferrar. "We want this to be a family-friendly event.As of early Sunday evening, 17 people were arrested at the parade, Boston police said. They did not specify exactly what they were arrested for.In the first nearly 30 minutes of the parade, MBTA Transit Police posted a photo on X of the number of alcoholic drinks confiscated at Broadway Station. Celtics star forward Jaylen Brown made an appearance at the parade on a float with his signature sneaker, 741. Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey posted a photo of herself and Lt. Gov. Kim Driscoll decked out in Dunkin' gear at the parade and the city's annual St. Patrick's Day Breakfast. Overall, the parade was one-of-a-kind, with Paul Revere riding on horseback and Revolutionary War minutemen being cheered by the crowd for running British redcoats out of town on Evacuation Day 250 years ago. "How do you explain this to Capitol Hill?" Massachusetts Rep. Stephen Lynch said. "I wish we could export this to Capitol Hill - people here are all having fun."
